That is strange.  Our CI runs the CUDA tests with this command:
```
python -m numba.runtests -m 4 numba.cuda.tests
```

This seems to depend on the order that tests are run in. Unfortunately I only realised this once the order of tests that reproduced the crash had already scrolled off my terminal. It seemed that editing files to start investigating adjusted the order in which tests ran, and the symptom disappeared. 

Hopefully this will pop back up again - I haven't been able to easily spot what influences the test loading / discovery / running order, but I wonder if on my system the `os.listdir`  (used in `numba.testing.__init__.load_testsuite` function is giving the files in a different order depending on the modification times of files and causing some differences.

**Update to this comment (9 Jan 2020) - I now no longer believe it's related to the order in which tests are run - later comments show the tests always running in the same order and it occurring / not occurring**

Later on, `(3)` runs and attempts to launch the `sum_reduce` kernel again, which leads to a segfault.

I think that:
* The `sum_reduce` kernel will have been cleared up because of the reset of the context.
* The test harness shouldn't interleave tests from different classes, at least if theyre a `CUDATestCase` (because these reset the context after every test).
